blogs.title: Wait, They're Coming Back? Navigating Biphasic and Multiphasic Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: A deep dive into the phenomenon of biphasic anaphylaxis, where symptoms recur after an initial resolution. This post discusses the unpredictable timing of relapses, the current lack of reliable predictors for recurrence, and the ongoing debate regarding the ideal observation window for high-risk patients.

blogs.title: The Auto-Injector Trap: Is 0.3mg Enough for Adults?
blogs.description: An analysis of the dosing gap between standard adult IM epinephrine recommendations (0.5mg) and the common 0.3mg auto-injectors. This post explores the clinical risk of underdosing adults over 50kg and how relying on auto-injectors in the ED might inadvertently lead to a need for repeated dosing or escalation of care.

blogs.title: Steroids for Anaphylaxis: Time to Stop the Habit?
blogs.description: For decades, corticosteroids have been used to prevent the 'second wave' of anaphylaxis. This post reviews the evidence (or lack thereof) supporting this practice, discussing recent systematic reviews that suggest steroids do not reduce the risk of biphasic reactions and may even be associated with increased ICU admissions.

blogs.title: Tryptase Timing: Getting the Diagnosis of Mastocytosis Right
blogs.description: A guide to the diagnostic workup of systemic mastocytosis. This post emphasizes the 'golden window' for tryptase sampling—comparing peak levels (1-2 hours post-onset) with baseline levels (24+ hours post-resolution)—and identifies the subtle clinical clues, like hepatomegaly and neuropsychiatric symptoms, that should trigger a mast cell workup.

blogs.title: Epi-Drip or Expectant? Managing the Multiphasic Nightmare
blogs.description: When a patient relapses multiple times, clinicians face a tension: start a continuous epinephrine infusion to pre-empt further episodes or remain expectant and treat reactively. This post discusses the management dilemmas and the risks associated with both strategies in the absence of formal guidelines for multiphasic courses.
